operations.comment: ; Named NES hardware, RAM and structure fields. Address-size prefixes preserve encoded widths.
; Indexed actor fields use strides 5 (traffic/secondary) and 4 (four-actor pool).
; high_score_base is indexed from 1 through 5 by the comparison/copy loop.
; work_value* bytes are shared rendering, collision and arithmetic temporaries; their interpretation is local to the routine.
; Scratch pointers are deliberately shared among graphics, dispatch and arithmetic helpers.
; Referenced table bases in the fixed PRG view. Physical tables are classified separately; CPU aliases do not change storage identity.
; Shared temporaries and newly resolved state/audio fields.
; Additional persistent, rendering and audio consumer fields.
; 16-byte iNES header: 32 KiB PRG, 32 KiB CHR, CNROM mapper 3, horizontal mirroring; no trainer. Header is separate from CPU/PPU storage.
; Disable interrupts and rendering, initialize the stack and persistent state, then enter the frame/state dispatcher. PRG mapping is fixed at physical banks 0,1,2,3; CHR selection is independent.
; Wait for the NMI frame latch, perform per-frame housekeeping, then tail-dispatch main_state through 23 little-endian handler addresses. Handlers return here rather than to a caller.
; Clear the NMI suppression flags and frame latch, then clear nametables and hide sprites.
; Unknown physical $007C..$0080 (end exclusive). Possible reset JMP plus a zero byte; no supported entry or format distinguishes code from stored data. Preserved verbatim.
; Consume the NMI frame latch. This busy wait requires NMI to be enabled and not gated off.
; Temporarily clear the PPU NMI-enable bit, wait for vblank, then restore the control shadow. Used around direct PPU transfers.
; Clear both logical nametables and hide all shadow OAM sprites.
; Write offscreen Y and zero tile/attributes/X for each of the 64 four-byte sprites in shadow OAM.
; Clear the two logical nametable pages beginning at PPU $2000 and $2800.
; Clear the logical nametable page at $2000; the adjacent entry uses $2800. Horizontal mirroring aliases physical pages.
; Clear 1024 PPU bytes from the selected nametable base, including attributes, then restore scroll/control registers.
; X:Y is a CPU source pointer, A chooses background zero or sprite nonzero palette base. Copy 16 bytes during vblank and reset the PPU address latch.
; Strobe both standard controllers and shift eight bits into scratch bytes; derive current, changed and newly pressed button masks. Bit order here puts Start at $08.
; Clear NMI-enable in the control shadow and both rendering bits in the mask shadow before changing PPU data.
; Restore scroll, enable NMI, wait one frame, then enable background and sprite rendering.
; Write X then Y to PPUADDR. Caller supplies a high/low PPU address with the latch synchronized.
; Restore the control shadow and both scroll bytes after a PPU transfer.
; X:Y points to a stream: little-endian PPU destination, tiles, $FE advances the destination by 32, $FF terminates. Restore scroll on exit.
; Set main_state from A and reset the two state-local timer bytes. Tail-dispatched handlers use this for transitions.
; Read and write the same ROM byte indexed by X to select CNROM CHR bank while respecting bus conflicts. Mapper byte is not a PRG bank index.
; Four bus-conflict-safe CNROM values $30..$33. Low two bits choose the physical CHR bank; PRG remains fixed.
; Save registers, acknowledge PPU status, and conditionally DMA shadow OAM and service queued graphics/audio work. Publish the frame latch and increment the NMI counter.
; Unknown physical $0238..$023C (end exclusive). Possible JSR $9209 / RTI wrapper; neither entry nor the adjacent second-RTS target has a supported contract. Preserved verbatim.
; 23 paired addresses indexed by main_state * 2; each handler owns its timer state.

; Initialize audio. Preserve score/options when the four-byte DECO signature matches; otherwise install defaults. Reset selection and enter state zero.
; Entry called by the main dispatcher; currently an immediate return. The following title initialization is a separate entry.
; Clear scroll and CHR selection, load title palettes and tile streams, build title sprites, and enter the title-wait state. PPU reads also stage tile-stream data through RAM.

; Title screen, attribute and sprite-text records. The title initializer supplies exact origins to the upload helpers; $FE advances a PPU row and $FF ends a stream. The leading address/value format differs from later tile streams; internal object names remain uncertain.
; Select the next title state and return to the frame dispatcher.
; Animate title palette triples every eight timer ticks; Start selects the configured course or begins the demonstration after timeout.
; Unknown physical $049E..$049F (end exclusive). Isolated RTI; interrupt entry and stack contract remain unresolved. Preserved verbatim.
; A is a controller mask and X is a valid course index (0..15). Keep X when masked
; pad1_current button is held; otherwise fall through to select course zero.
; Both paths join the existing course-store/new-game initializer. The actual
; caller and natural selection of this conditional entry remain unknown.
; Reset course/start flags and clear the display before entering new-game initialization.
; Mark demonstration mode, reset its controller sequence, then enter the same initialization path.
; Two 16-byte title palettes followed by six animation colors (two triples). TitleWaitAndStart alternates the triple index between zero and three.
; Install the initial life count, clear decimal score digits and award tracking, and enter course selection.
; Copy the selected starting course; choose the demonstration or ordinary intro state from the mode flag.
; Display two sprite text streams once, wait to timer $80, then enter course setup.
; Two sprite-text records for the player/start screen: Y, X, tile bytes, $FF. Their origins are independently selected by the intro handler.
; Clear route, time, scroll and bonus state. Initialize decimal time digits and enter course graphics setup.
; Choose CHR bank and background/sprite palettes for the course; copy the background palette into RAM, reset player/status flags, then enter actor setup.
; Sixteen course-indexed CHR/theme choices, each in 0..3. This domain is independent of the fixed PRG bank context.
; Initialize three five-byte actors, two additional five-byte actors and four four-byte actors from course selectors. Reset transient objects and select intro or demonstration flow.
; Build course/lives sprite text on first tick, draw the player and HUD, then wait until timer $80 before entering road setup.
; Scene sprite-text record followed by sixteen digit tile IDs used when drawing the course number. Text uses Y, X, tiles and an $FF terminator.
; Disable rendering, build road and collision caches, place the player, render its initial sprite, then enter the pre-race animation.
; Animate the pre-race sprite block and queue the course sound. On completion set the driving state and publish graphics updates.
; Sixteen course-indexed audio command IDs used when entering driving. They select the command-header table, not executable PRG banks.
; Read input, handle demo exit/pause, update HUD, collisions, player and traffic, advance road data, then publish graphics work. NMI work is gated while mutable state is being assembled.
; Alternate gameplay frame path with a reduced collision/object update sequence; shares road, HUD and sprite services with ordinary driving.
; Start a timed palette animation, then clear the screen, build a special road/player scene and enter its inner transition dispatcher.
; Two 16-byte transition palettes selected by BeginTransitionFrame before the five-state inner dispatcher starts.

; Cycle palette entries with a short hold, queue a sound when appropriate, then dispatch on the low nibble of transition_state. The low nibble has five handlers; bits 4..6 select eight text phases before the final departure states.
; Move the player upward two pixels per frame; at Y<$60 advance the inner state and start a $60-tick hold.
; Count the hold down, advance the low-nibble state, clear phase bits and start the eight-message sequence with sound $0B.
; High state bits select one of eight sprite-text pointers. Every $80 ticks hide the previous text and advance phase; overflow enters state 3.
; Reset the departure hold and hide the player OAM group before proceeding to the shared draw path.
; Draw the fixed departure message, then hide both OAM groups, add five time units and sound command 2 when its hold expires.
; Move upward two pixels each frame. Count the final hold only while Y is within $80..$EF; expiry selects main state $10.
; Hide the player OAM group and blink the prompt according to timer bit 3.
; Read controllers; a newly pressed bit 0 calls the decimal time increment helper before rendering.
; Draw player sprites, copy their OAM buffer and draw time digits, advance the main timer and return to the frame dispatcher.
; Hide twelve OAM sprites at offsets $90..$BC. Other OAM groups remain untouched.
; Hide sixteen OAM sprites at offsets $C0..$FC before replacing a text panel.
; Add five to the middle decimal time digit, carrying into the high digit at ten.

; Five transition handler words, eight text pointers and their $FF-terminated sprite-text records, followed by six palette triples. Low state nibble selects the handler; bits 4..6 select the text; transition_palette_index selects a triple.

; transition selector 1

; transition selector 4
; Clear transition state, select course CHR bank and reenter course graphics setup.
; Initialize finish sound/flags once, continue HUD/sprite updates and wait roughly $180 ticks before entering the result state.
; Convert remaining time into score while time is nonzero. Then draw the results, add decimal bonus digits, advance course and restart setup; course boundaries clear the route flag.
; Four result-screen sprite-text records, each Y, X, tiles, $FF. CourseResultsFrame supplies each origin explicitly.
; Subtract one from the packed decimal life count outside demo mode. Choose game-over or course restart, preserving the special last-course route and minimum time behavior.
; Draw game-over streams on first tick; accept Start or timeout, track a controller selection mask, then return to title initialization.
; Two game-over sprite-text records selected by GameOverFrame. Both end at $FF before the ending initializer.
; Select ending CHR bank, construct background/palettes and sprite scene, queue sound, then select ending animation state 22.
; Two 16-byte rescue-ending palettes, background then sprite, loaded by InitializeRescueEnding.

; Alternate two palette entries every 16 ticks, then tail-dispatch through the ending selector in RAM $0500. The selector advances through four handlers: approach, rescue group, 21 text rows and final return delay.
; Draw two pairs of alternating metasprites and move their X positions together every other tick. Advance the ending selector when the right group reaches $78.
; Place five fixed metasprites in OAM, then count the delay before entering text state 2 and resetting its row index.
; Display 21 bounded sprite-text records, using a parallel OAM-offset table. Advance one row per $20 ticks; after row 10 wait and clear the screen, after row 20 advance state.
; Wait 128 NMI frames, then disable rendering and clear the previous text panel before continuing.
; Advance the ending selector after the final text row; shared drawing continues through the dispatcher exit.
; Count the final delay, clear the starting-course option and select main state 4. No natural full-game route is implied.
; Increment the state-local timer and return to the frame dispatcher.
; Four ending handler words, 21 OAM offsets, 21 text pointers and 21 Y/X/tile/$FF records. ending_text_index stops at $15; this terminal selector is not a 22nd text row.
; ending selector 0
; ending selector 1
; ending selector 2
; ending selector 3
; Zero both scroll bytes and clear the vertical nametable select bit in the control shadow.
; Scan eight pending-work bits and call handlers through a table using a synthetic return address. Clear both request masks afterward, then update audio.
; Restore saved work index and remaining mask after an indirect work handler returns.
; Advance the eight-entry work scan, clear request masks and run audio at completion.
; Eight NMI work-handler words. Slot zero uploads road graphics; seven slots return through the supported no-op entry. The neighboring second RTS has no supported structural role.

; Return immediately for the seven unimplemented NMI-work slots; the adjacent second RTS remains structurally unresolved.
; Unknown physical $1219..$121A (end exclusive). Second bare RTS next to the supported NMI no-op. Its only proposed caller is itself structurally ambiguous. Preserved verbatim.
; Upload four 2x2 tile blocks and two attribute bytes until four slices are done. Apply vertical nametable wrapping and advance scroll by the low-nibble speed.
; Cycle eight prerecorded button masks, holding each for $60 ticks; substitute them for player current/newly pressed input.
; Eight synthetic controller masks selected by demo_input_index&7. Bit meanings match ReadControllers; these bytes are input data.
; Detect a fresh Start edge, queue pause sound and wait for audio acceptance; poll until a second fresh Start edge, then queue resume sound.
; For three five-byte actors, test low-nibble activity and coordinate proximity. Set opposing direction bits, collision states and timers, with road flags modifying the response.
; Find a colliding actor and compare it against the other three slots using two coordinate windows; set opposing movement flags and response timers on both records.
; Rotate a three-actor cursor. Compare its coordinates with traffic and two extra objects, setting state $0A and a direction bit on overlap.

; Age the player cooldown and clear its status bit when it expires; dispatch on the player's low-nibble state. Sixteen update words cover the low-nibble selector; two following words belong to the separate collision-sample dispatch.
; Continue into the classified player environment/motion handler; intervening bytes remain unclassified.
; Clear the player's low state nibble and fall into the existing environment/movement path; directional high bits survive.
; Track tile-cell changes, sample two points around the player, and resolve map flags through terrain handlers or accumulated masks. Coordinates use a 17-row ring cache.
; Synthetic RTS continuation: the caller pushed $9662. Preserve the inherited zero flag across three NOPs; nonzero collision selects state 9 or 12, starts a $20-tick reaction and stops road motion.
; Convert the terrain high nibble to one of two bit masks, process the second sample, and continue player state/motion checks. A jump button may initiate state 5 when allowed.
; After the reaction timer, inspect the four stride-4 actors when their pool is active. Proximity selects recovery state 7; otherwise advance to the next timed state.
; Keep directional bits, select low state 7, install a $10-tick timer and play command 7.
; Advance the low player state after $20 ticks and play command 3; preserve the shared end-of-update path.
; While the pool is active, test each idle actor against a 48-by-48 window. Mark hits, add score and update the target count; completing the required count can spawn the exit and award a bonus.
; On timer expiry select state 1, clear the temporary mode flags, reset vertical phase and resume ordinary movement.
; On alternating ticks adjust vertical position within $A0..$C0; horizontal direction buttons adjust the other coordinate. Continue at the shared player return.
; Tail-route shared player states 8..10 to the timed reaction path; no independent movement is performed here.
; Tail-route state 11 to the next timed exit reaction.
; Count the player timer, advance state on expiry and reload $20 ticks.
; When the timer expires choose low state 15 and a $60-tick delay.
; Count the final reaction timer; expiry selects main state $13.
; Shared return for the player-state handlers.

; Sixteen player update words selected by the low state nibble, then two tile-shape sample handlers selected by collision_sample_index 0 or 1. The collision caller pushes a synthetic return for PlayerAfterCollisionSamples.

; Scan fourteen bits across two terrain masks and tail-dispatch the first selected effect. The handlers either continue scanning, enter a transition, initialize a vertical/target mode or set a player flag; precise terrain artwork names remain uncertain.
; Return to the terrain-bit scanner without changing state. Multiple terrain bits intentionally share this handler.
; Alias entry for the jump/transition terrain response.
; Award the shared score/effect and select main state $11, then return to the terrain scanner.
; Only on the first contact set vertical-mode bit 7, award the shared effect and play sound $0B.
; Only once set target-sequence bit 7, choose a variant from game_tick&7, merge a count of 1..4 and reset the hit counter. Set control bit $20 for the sequence.
; Set player flag $20 and return to the common bit-scan continuation.

; Add the small score award and start a transient effect at the player's Y and X+$20 with a $20-tick life.
; Dispatch on the low nibble of the auxiliary object state through paired addresses.

; On alternate ticks approach the player, constrain Y around $A0..$BF and X to $50..$C0, and cycle direction bits. A close contact either rebounds both participants or, after ten state-1 hits, starts defeat state 2.
; Use bounded Y/X differences to derive contact direction. Only player states below 3 participate; state 1 accumulates the defeat hit count.
; Store the contact direction in auxiliary state 1 and its opposite in player state 2; both receive $20-tick reaction timers.
; Move one pixel along each stored contact direction, reversing horizontal direction at bounds. Count the reaction down, then return to chasing state 0.
; Apply the common deceleration helper. Once speed falls below $21, select state 3 and stop the road.
; Use a $10-tick next-state delay for states 3 and 4; both share the countdown body.
; Use a $80-tick next-state delay for state 5.
; On expiry advance the low state, install the supplied delay and play command 7.
; After the final countdown select main state $15, the rescue-ending initializer.
; Shared auxiliary-handler return.
; Seven auxiliary update words. Chase/contact, rebound, defeat slowdown, two shared short countdowns, long countdown and ending transition form the supported state graph.

; Apply controller acceleration/braking and road restrictions, derive scroll speed, update jump eligibility and convert speed to three display digits. Units are game-internal.
; Increase the speed accumulator up to $7F.
; Decrease the speed accumulator when at least $20.
; Count down an active transient effect and clear its state on expiry.
; Every $20 eligible ticks decrement the three-digit decimal timer; suppress decrement when the road stop flag is set.
; Increment the three decimal digits time_units..time_hundreds, propagating carry left and wrapping 999 to 000. Independent static contract; a natural caller is not asserted.
; Subtract one from the three unpacked decimal digits, borrowing at zero and saturating the high digit at zero.
; Coordinate actor-group activation and handover, cycling variants and initializing four four-byte slots when the group changes.
; Check whether all traffic slots reached state 9, otherwise prepare ring-map coordinates and dispatch each actor's low-nibble state. Inner handlers are partly unclassified.
; Shared steering entry: subtract four from current traffic X, then apply road motion.

; Recycle out-of-range slots with a course-allowed type, spawn Y and fixed X. Otherwise inspect two collision-map samples, steer by four pixels toward an open side, then dispatch normal movement or the slot's reaction state.
; Search the circular three-bit type selector until the course mask permits it. Current masks exclude type 7; seven movement words must not include the spawn-Y bytes.
; Read the high collision nibble at the slot's left and right edges; if blocked, also test adjacent cells to choose an escape side.
; For a normal slot subtract the road-dependent speed contribution, then dispatch its bounded movement type. Active reaction states use the shared lateral-motion path.
; Alias movement entry for the oscillating drift type.
; Alias movement entry for the bounded chase type.
; On odd ticks move down and sideways; reverse the lateral direction every $60 ticks.
; Bounce vertically between the local limits and approach player X once every four ticks.
; While player state is zero and the timer permits, approach Y and X on alternate ticks; count the movement timer down.
; Move the current slot upward one pixel, then continue the three-slot iterator.
; Move four pixels in the stored horizontal direction, clear the low reaction nibble and finish the slot.
; Read both collision samples through the shared tile-shape predicates. A hit selects state 2 or 5 from the tile's high nibble and starts a five-tick timer with matching sound.
; Count the rebound timer, choose its next state from player flag 4 on expiry and otherwise move along stored direction bits.
; Alias entry for the delayed score reaction.
; Alias entry for the subsequent disappearance delay.
; Skip this slot without motion.
; After five ticks advance the state, award score and increment the crash count, then apply road motion.
; After its short timer enter state 7 with a $20-tick hold.
; Count the vanish timer when nonzero; no position update in this state.
; Skip road-relative motion when the road-stop bit is set.
; Add the road speed to slot Y, hide/recycle slots beyond $E0 and check whether the collision-map cell permits resetting state.
; Map the slot back into the 17-row collision ring. A zero high nibble clears the low state; occupied road cells preserve it.
; Advance the stride-5 offset and three-slot counter, returning to dispatch until all three slots are handled.
; Shared return from the traffic dispatch paths.

; Eleven traffic-state words, seven movement-type words and seven spawn-Y bytes. Course masks are all $7F, so normal type selection excludes 7. The separate eight-entry sprite table still explicitly defines type 7.

; Derive the contact direction from bounded Y/X differences. Player state 1 awards score and selects a timed secondary reaction; player flag 4 instead repels the secondary, otherwise the player enters state 2.
; Inspect both collision-map edges and adjacent cells to steer four pixels toward an opening, sharing the collision-ring format with traffic.

; A state-1 slot counts its rebound timer and moves by direction bits; other states separate the two slots before type movement. One directional branch writes traffic_y,X exactly as encoded; do not silently correct it.
; Compare the two stride-5 slots and push the current slot four pixels away horizontally while their windows overlap.
; Subtract the road-dependent speed contribution before entering the four-type movement dispatch.
; On odd ticks move down one pixel, then finish the slot.

; When player/slot geometry and object availability permit, copy the slot's position into the special object and start state 5. Direction comes from the four-type table; matching score digits select an alternate mode. Otherwise drift upward on odd ticks.
; On odd ticks move up one pixel, then finish the slot.
; On timer expiry advance state and install a five-tick delay; apply road motion while waiting.
; On timer expiry advance state, install $20 ticks and increment the crash count.
; Count the current timer when nonzero and finish without position changes.
; Wait out the timer and for four-actor/pickup/exit objects to become free. Then reset the secondary and activate the special object's high bit with sound $0E.
; Skip this slot unchanged.
; Skip road motion when the stop bit is set.
; Advance Y by road speed; recycle past $E0 with the course-pair timer. Otherwise wait for an empty collision cell and expired timer before clearing the state.
; Translate Y into the 17-row ring and test the high collision nibble. Count the remaining timer only when the cell is clear.
; Advance the stride-5 slot offset. The second slot is updated only from course 4 onward; return after both slots.
